newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch spending pickup buoys Vendex H1 net.
newsitem.headline: Dutch spending pickup buoys Vendex H1 net.

text.p: Retail and services group Vendex International NV said on Tuesday profits rose 21 percent in the first half and were on course to increase further if the recent upturn in consumer spending held up over the second half.
Chairman Jan-Michiel Hessels was upbeat about the Dutch group's performance and added the firm was on course for a 10 percent annual rise in operating earnings.

"The most important thing is that (Vendex) is back on track for a 10 percent annual increase in EBIT (earnings before interest and tax) excluding property," Hessels said at a press conference to announce the results.

Net profit rose to 151 million guilders ($89.9 million) in the six months to July 31 from 125 million a year ago and operating income rose 19 percent to 153 million. Excluding the redevelopment and sale of property, which in the past has contributed more to results than trading, operating income rose 22 percent.
The figures, released before the start of bourse trading, were almost in line with analysts' consensus.
On the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, Vendex shares opened 1.40 guilders higher at 63.10 but later pared their gains to trade up 60 cents at 62.30 by 1050 GMT.

Vendex said it was too early to make a firm earnings forecast over the full year, but added it expected higher operating profits in its three main activities over the full year if the recent upturn in consumer spending continued.
"In addition to the already envisaged increase in the food and services sectors, operating income will also shown an increase in the non-food retail trade," it said in a statement.
Hessels said he saw particular potential for profit improvement in the group's non-food sector.

"Temporary employment will double over the next five years for a number of reasons and I see particular potential for profit improvement in the non-food sector in specialty and department stores," he said.

Property is still the main support for the group's flagship department store chain Vroom & Dreesmann. Discounting these activities, the chain posted an operating loss -- albeit smaller than last year -- of 11 million guilders versus 13 million.
Vendex said a surge in sales of fashion clothing in the second quarter had helped the store chain hold turnover steady, and buoyed the result at its specialty store activities.
Hessels said longer shop opening hours in the Netherlands had a marginal affect on sales in the first half of the year, since liberalised hours were only introduced in June.
"The second half impact will be considerably bigger in both food and non-food," he said.
Temporary employment services boosted profits due to internal growth and acquisitions. Alongside its home market, the group is active in Belgium, France, Germany and Spain.

"Market share was increased in Belgium as well as in the declining French market," the group said. But the Netherlands was the major motor behind the 7.7 percent increase in operating profits to 28 million guilders.

Maintenance services booked 18 percent higher sales due to the acquisition midway through last year of French cleaning agency Bis Propriete. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040 ($ = 1.679 Dutch Guilders)
